page: OVHcloud a10-180 is a high-density GPU-accelerated cloud server deployed on KVM virtualization within the Cloud GPU family. The system is powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9554 processor featuring 120 dedicated physical cores clocked at 3.3 GHz, operating with hyperthreading disabled to dedicate one thread per core. Memory capacity is provisioned at 170 GB, yielding a compact ratio of 1.42 GB of RAM per core. Hardware acceleration is delivered via four dedicated NVIDIA Ampere A10 GPUs, providing an aggregate 96 GB of GDDR6 VRAM. Storage is supplied through a local 400 GB SSD, supported by a 25 Gbps baseline network interface. Public IPv4 connectivity is not included complimentary.

Benchmark results highlight extreme multi-threaded computational capabilities alongside strong AI inference throughput. The instance achieves top-decile performance in multi-core metrics, registering 199,580.72 in stress-ng multi-core tests and a PassMark CPU score of 99,328.26. Hardware vector execution is strengthened by full AVX-512 instruction support, reflected in top-tier ratings for PassMark extended instructions and Clang software compilation. In synthetic throughput benchmarks, Redis SET operations reached 151.11 million operations per second. Large language model evaluation reveals prompt processing speeds of 2,799.26 tokens per second on 7B parameter models and 330.75 tokens per second on 70B models, with text generation scaling from 90.14 tokens per second on 7B down to 10.73 tokens per second on 70B weights across the four A10 GPUs.

The hardware configuration trades excessive RAM allocations to prioritize raw compute density and multi-GPU parallelization. With 1.42 GB of system memory per core, the machine is not tailored for large in-memory databases or virtualization hosts requiring extensive RAM per thread. However, aggregating four enterprise-grade A10 GPUs with 120 dedicated AMD Zen 4 cores provides high cost efficiency for GPU-bound execution pipelines where renting larger A100 or H100 clusters would result in unused resource overhead. OVHcloud a10-180 is optimal for distributed deep learning inference, batch image and video processing, ray tracing, parallel compilation workloads, and high-concurrency numeric simulations.
description: OVHcloud a10-180 is a GPU-accelerated compute instance engineered for high-throughput machine learning inference and parallel processing tasks. Driven by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9554 processor delivering 120 dedicated physical cores at 3.3 GHz without multi-threading, the instance includes 170 GB of system memory, yielding 1.42 GB per core. Acceleration is provided by four bundled NVIDIA Ampere A10 GPUs offering a combined 96 GB of VRAM. Storage consists of a local 400 GB SSD, complemented by a 25 Gbps baseline network link. Benchmark evaluations demonstrate exceptional multi-threaded performance, with PassMark CPU and stress-ng multi-core metrics placing in the top ten percent, alongside high-throughput Clang software compilation and Redis operations. The system sustains robust large language model token processing across 7B and 70B parameter profiles. While the memory-to-core ratio limits memory-intensive virtualization, this instance provides dense computational density suited for deep learning inference, batch video and image rendering, and high-concurrency scientific simulations.
